i mentioned a p2p voat concept a couple of times - never got any feedback from the devs so i assume there is no interest, which is unfortunate because i think distributed apps might be the only way to maintain freedom in a www that is continuing to fall under government/corporate control/censorship

So, aside from legal risks, how would it work? I'm not arguing against it, I'm legitimately curious how it would flow.

If you make a post, it could take days for that post to update across the network, unless you had data hubs that all of the node-hosts pointed to. I don't think it would be viable for each each node to host the data as well as the code that renders it.

There would have to be several node producing feeds from the data to serve out to the final nodes.

Perhaps it could be sub based? For example, I only grab feeds for subs I'm subscribed to. Anyone near me that is also subscribed to those nodes could pull a feed from me. That could also allow some protection against things that might be risky. That would still mean that it might take time for a post to filter all the way through the net to each node.
We could call it the Users' Network, or Usenet for short.

I think that something like what your talking about could better implemented using something like websockets

Websockets allow for server and client communication, which gives us a way to "refresh" the "page". So with that level of communication we would then only need a way to distribute the "files" of the site. We could use something like the bittorrent protocol to send this data, however we would still want to have some kind of central location where the information is sent first then pushed out to the clients. We could setup "miners" like you mentioned but they would be more like repos, and we could encrypt all that data on a repo using something like the block chain protocol. This would promote consistency and transparency, however it would likely require a good amount of work to get this working correctly. There could be two types of clients, one that hosts data and one that consumes it. This could be a lot like the Aether though, I have not read more about it other than the front page on their site.
